MUQATIL:2:261-262/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:261-262/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:261-262/r2.claim: The promise of reward without fear or grief was revealed about Uthman, for his Tabuk expenditure and purchase of the Ruma well for Muslims.

MUQATIL:2:261-262/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:261-262/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:261-262/r3.claim: It was also revealed about Abd al-Rahman b. Awf, who gave four thousand dirhams, half his wealth.

TAB-FULL:v4p655/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r1.claim: The verse concerns giving wealth to equip and support fighters against God’s enemies, including their transport and other needs.

TAB-FULL:v4p655/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r2.claim: Reminding recipients means displaying one’s favor by words or actions; harm includes complaining that they failed their duty in battle.

TAB-FULL:v4p655/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r3.claim: A donor supporting jihad seeks God’s reward, so the recipient owes no favor in return; the donor’s recompense is from God.

TAB-FULL:v4p655/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r4.claim: Qatada says God knew some people would remind others of their gifts, so He warned against it and cited the next verse.

TAB-FULL:v4p655/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the condition against reminders applies to those who stay back and fund fighters; the fighters themselves were not given that condition.

TAB-FULL:v4p655/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p655/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts his father’s advice to withhold even a greeting if it would burden a fighter, and a rebuke to a woman whose offer had already insulted the fighters.

TAB-FULL:v4p657/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p657/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p657/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says it is better not to spend than to spend and then follow the gift with reminders or harm.

TAB-FULL:v4p657/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p657/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p657/r2.claim: The promised wage is the recompense for spending in God’s cause without reminders or harm.

TAB-FULL:v4p657/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p657/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p657/r3.claim: Those donors face no fear when they meet God, leave worldly life, or encounter the terrors of resurrection, and they do not grieve over what they left behind.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p516/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p516/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p516/r1.claim: Al-Hasan describes people who send someone on an expedition or support a recipient, then remind and hurt them by boasting of their spending; such reminders are not counted as sincerely seeking God's reward.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p516/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p516/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p516/r2.claim: Qatada says God knew some people would remind others of their gifts and disliked that behavior.

THALABI:v2p258/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p258/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p258/r7.claim: Following a gift with mann means reminding its recipient of it, recounting favors, or repeatedly making the gift a reproach; the root first meant to bestow.

THALABI:v2p258/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p258/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p258/r8.claim: Man derives from giving or bestowing; the word came to mean recalling and claiming credit for a favor.

THALABI:v2p258/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p258/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p258/r9.claim: Harm includes publicizing a gift to someone who need not know of it and other hurtful speech.

THALABI:v2p259/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r1.speaker: سفيان والمفضل
THALABI:v2p259/r1.claim: Sufyān and al-Mufaḍḍal explain mann and harm as saying, “I gave you, but you did not thank me.”

THALABI:v2p259/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r2.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v2p259/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it is better not to give than to give and then follow the gift with reproach and harm.

THALABI:v2p259/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v2p259/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd reports his father advising donors to withhold even a greeting if they think it will burden the recipient.

THALABI:v2p259/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v2p259/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that his father rebuked a woman who suspected men going to jihad only wanted fruit; her words had hurt them before she gave them a quiver and arrows.

THALABI:v2p259/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p259/r5.claim: God reserves mann as an attribute of grace: human reminders taunt and spoil a gift, whereas God's mention of a blessing is beneficence and favor.

THALABI:v2p259/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r6.speaker: معاد بن المثنى عن أبيه محمود بن الوراق
THALABI:v2p259/r6.claim: A poem attributed to Maʿād ibn al-Muthannā, from his father Maḥmūd ibn al-Warrāq, praises a good deed free from reproach.

THALABI:v2p259/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r7.speaker: أبو ذر القرطبي
THALABI:v2p259/r7.claim: A poem transmitted by Abū Dharr al-Qurṭubī warns that reminding people of a favor diminishes it and spoils the giver's generosity.

THALABI:v2p259/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r8.speaker: محمد بن طاهر عن أبي علي البصري
THALABI:v2p259/r8.claim: A poem describes a recipient turning hostile to a benefactor when the benefactor's fortunes later decline.

THALABI:v2p259/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p259/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p259/r9.claim: Another poem says that reproach ruins the good already done and that a generous person does not remind others of gifts.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r1.claim: Reminding a recipient means saying one did good to or supported them; harm includes reproaching them for perpetual poverty or blaming them for one's hardship.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r2.claim: Their promised reward is what they earned through the Lord's promise for their spending.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r3.claim: Having no fear means either not fearing the loss of reward or not fearing the terrors of the afterlife.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r4.claim: Having no sorrow means not grieving either what they spent or what they left behind.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r5.claim: One report says this verse was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan's spending on the Army of Hardship during the Tabuk expedition.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī’s account identifies ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf among those addressed: he donated four thousand dirhams, half of his savings, as a loan to God.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r2.speaker: عثمان رضي الله عنه
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r2.claim: The account says ʿUthmān equipped the Tabūk expedition with a thousand camels and donated the well of Rumah; the verse was revealed about him and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p87/r3.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says he saw the Prophet pray for ʿUthmān through dawn, asking God to be pleased with him; the source connects the verse to ʿUthmān.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r1.claim: Mann can mean a gift or benefaction; a prophetic statement calls Abu Bakr the most generous in companionship and wealth, and God is called Mannān because He gives without seeking repayment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r2.claim: Mann can also mean reducing or withholding a due; 68:3 says a reward is not cut off or diminished, and death is called manūn because it cuts lives short.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r3.claim: The blameworthy mann here is reminding a recipient of one's favor and thereby spoiling it; a cited poem illustrates that even a small gift can be ruined by reproach.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r4.claim: Arabs praise benefactors who leave their kindness unmentioned, as in the quoted poem about a great favor kept hidden by its giver.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r5.claim: Mann is telling the recipient that one improved, rescued, or supported him through one's generosity.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p408/r6.claim: Harm is mentioning one's favor to a recipient who dislikes being reminded of it, or any similarly hurtful remark.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:261-263/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:261-263/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:261-263/r2.claim: Mann is reminding the recipient of one's generosity, such as claiming to have helped, strengthened, or repaired the person's deficiency.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:261-263/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:261-263/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:261-263/r3.claim: Harm means disclosing one's favor to someone who dislikes being reminded of the benefactor's help.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Uthman and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: the latter gave four thousand dirhams and retained four thousand for his family, and Uthman equipped the Tabuk army with a thousand camels.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سمرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r2.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura reports that Uthman brought a thousand dinars for the army of hardship; the Prophet turned them over and said Ibn Affan's deeds would not harm him after that day.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r3.claim: Man is reminding the recipient of one's gift and enumerating one's favors so as to spoil them; harm includes reproaching or saying the recipient keeps asking and causing annoyance.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r4.speaker: سفيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r4.claim: Sufyan says harm includes telling a recipient, 'I gave you and gave you; you were not grateful.'

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r5.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd relays his father's advice to stop greeting a recipient if one's greeting burdens him; God forbids reminding people of favors, a reproach among humans but a divine favor and reminder from God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p325/r6.claim: Those who give without reminding or harming receive their reward from God and have neither fear nor grief.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r1.claim: Man is to remind the recipient of his favor and claim that he created an obligation; Arab advice says to forget good deeds, as a poem warns.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r2.claim: Harm means acting superior to the recipient because of what one gave; a proverb contrasts the sweetness of generosity with the bitterness of reminding someone.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r3.claim: Then marks the gap between giving and refraining from reminders: refraining is better than the act of giving itself, just as steadfastness is better than entering faith.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p338#3/r4.claim: The first clause lacks fa because its relative does not imply a condition; in the later clause, fa signals that giving earns the reward, a link absent without it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p355#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p355#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p355#2/r14.claim: The following verse limits the reward to spenders who do not follow their gift with reproach or harm; a donor may give for God’s reward, for compensation from the recipient, or under pressure, and the latter motives can lead to reproach or injury.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r1.claim: Reproach and injury expose that the donor was motivated by self-interest rather than sincerity; they invalidate that gift because they show it was not truly charity, but do not nullify separate sincere gifts.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r10.claim: The promised reward is Paradise; after death the giver has no fear about what lies ahead and no grief over worldly losses because he rejoices in the afterlife.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r2.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r2.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says the verse was reportedly revealed about ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r3.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r3.claim: Another reported occasion identifies ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r4.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r4.claim: Makkī reports that the verse concerned ʿUthmān and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r5.claim: Mann is recounting a favor in order to enumerate and reproach the recipient; injury means insult or complaint and is broader, but mann is singled out because it commonly occurs.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd assigns the preceding verse to those who fight with their wealth and this one to people who stay home and give; he says only the latter verse stipulates no reproach.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya sees no sound basis for Ibn Zayd’s distinction, calling it an unsupported assertion.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam advises a donor not to greet the recipient if the greeting itself would burden someone to whom he gave for God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r9.speaker: امرأة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p356/r9.claim: A woman asks Abū Usāma for a truly committed fighter, suspects they fight only for fruit, and is rebuked for having hurt them before giving.

TABRISI:2:262#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:262#2/r1.speaker: محمد
TABRISI:2:262#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says that the person who reminds others of a gift will not be addressed, regarded, or purified by God and will suffer painful punishment.

TABRISI:2:262/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:262/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:262/r1.claim: Mann is reminding a recipient of a favor in a way that spoils it; its root means cutting off, as in an uncut reward or a frayed rope.

TABRISI:2:262/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:262/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:262/r2.claim: Harm is injury that reaches its target; fear anticipates harm, and grief is distress that weighs heavily on the self.

TABRISI:2:262/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:262/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:262/r3.claim: After commanding spending, God describes proper giving as one that is not followed by reminders or injury; reminders include saying I gave you this or rescued you.

TABRISI:2:262/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:262/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:262/r4.claim: Harm may be insulting the recipient, frowning at him, burdening him with work, or diverting him to the donor's tasks; all spoil the gift and its reward.

TABRISI:2:262/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:262/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:262/r5.claim: Their reward is recompense with God, secure from loss or diminution; the phrase at their Lord reassures the soul that what is with God cannot vanish.

TABRISI:2:262/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:262/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:262/r6.claim: The verse makes the promise conditional: reward is deserved if spending is not followed by reminders or harm; without that condition, entitlement to reward does not follow.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r1.speaker: ابن السائب ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Uthman's spending at Tabuk and gift of the well of Rumah to Muslims, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf giving four thousand dirhams, half his wealth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r2.claim: Mann is reminding a poor recipient, “I helped and supported you,” in a boastful way.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r3.claim: Another view takes mann as claiming credit against God for giving charity.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r4.claim: The praiseworthy mann means conferring a blessing, as with God’s favor; blameworthy mann means treating a gift as great and boasting about it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r5.claim: The accompanying poem about “giving little then quickly boasting” illustrates the blameworthy meaning of mann.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r6.claim: Harm includes insulting the poor recipient or telling others about a gift when the recipient dislikes that disclosure; both hurt the recipient and contradict sincere charity.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r7.speaker: حسان بن سنان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p316#3/r7.claim: Hasan ibn Sinan bought and freed a man's household without identifying himself or telling them who he was.

RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r1.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Uthman and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: Uthman equipped the Tabuk expedition with a thousand camels and a thousand dinars, while Abd al-Rahman gave half his wealth, four thousand dinars.

RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r2.claim: The Prophet prayed that God be pleased with Uthman after his contribution.

RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r3.claim: Some commentators distinguish the previous verse as spending on oneself and this verse as spending on others, whose reward requires no taunting or harm.

RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r4.claim: Al-Qaffal says the condition also covers someone spending on himself to join the Prophet and Muslims in jihad: he must not boast to them or insult fellow believers.

RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r5.claim: Minn can mean benefaction; Ibn al-Anbari cites a poem asking someone to favor the speaker with a greeting, and the Prophet called Abu Bakr the most generous companion in wealth.

RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p40/r6.claim: Minn can also mean diminishing or withholding; the Quran describes a reward as غير ممنون, and death is called manun because it cuts lives short.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r1.claim: The wording requires avoiding both taunt and harm in the sense that neither may occur; the reward is not preserved merely by avoiding one while committing the other.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r2.claim: The Mu'tazila infer that major sins cancel reward, since the promised reward remains only when minn and adhā are absent.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi's school says taunting and harm show the gift was given for self-exaltation, not God's pleasure, so it never earned reward in the first place.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r4.claim: Al-Qadi objects that ثم makes taunting later than a valid act of giving, which should already have earned reward because a condition must exist when its cause occurs.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r5.claim: The response is that later taunting reveals the original gift was made for status, not God; alternatively, a later opposing event may prevent an earlier act from taking effect, as in the doctrine of ultimate outcome.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r6.claim: The verse indicates that both taunting and harm are major sins because either one strips this great act of its promised reward.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p41#2/r7.claim: The Mu'tazila say the servant's action makes God owe him reward; al-Razi's school says reward comes through God's promise, since performing an obligation does not itself earn payment.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r1.claim: The blameworthy minn is publicizing one's benefaction, while adhā is reproaching the recipient because of what was given.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r2.claim: Taunting deepens the needy recipient's humiliation and turns a prior benefit into harm after the giver has helped him.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r3.claim: Publicizing generosity discourages people in need from seeking the giver's charity.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r4.claim: A giver should recognize the gift as God's favor, be grateful for being enabled to give, and fear that some accompanying behavior may prevent acceptance.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r5.claim: The deeper reason is that God prepared the means of giving and removed its obstacles, so God is the true giver; fixating on visible causes instead of God leaves one at an animal level.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r6.claim: Adhā here should mean the reproach attached to the gift, not every hurt to a believer; an example is telling the poor person that his visits distress the giver.

RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p41/r7.claim: One who gives without either taunt or harm receives great reward and abundant recompense.

RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r1.claim: Al-Razi's school argues this verse disproves cancellation of reward because it states without qualification that the spenders have their reward, even after grave sins.

RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r2.speaker: الأمة
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r2.claim: The community agrees that having their reward with their Lord is conditioned on not committing unbelief; this shows a general expression may intend a restricted class.

RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r3.claim: Since general wording may be restricted, general texts cannot provide categorical proof for the Mu'tazili doctrine of irrevocable threats.

RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r4.claim: One reading says their spending is not wasted: its reward will be fully delivered on the Day of Resurrection, so they neither fear nor grieve over losing it.

RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p42/r5.claim: A second reading is that they will not fear punishment on the Day of Resurrection, as in the assurances in 27:89 and 21:103.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r1.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r1.claim: Moved by the warning that the recipient stands between two outcomes, Umar wept and gave his shirt for the Day of Judgment, not because of the poem.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r10.claim: Harm includes insults and complaints; it is broader than mann, which is singled out because it commonly occurs and is one form of harm.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd advises a donor who thinks even greeting the recipient burdens him to refrain from greeting him.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r12.speaker: أبو أسامة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r12.claim: When a woman disparaged fighters as going out to eat fruit and offered arrows and a quiver, Abu Usama said she had harmed them before giving.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r13.claim: A donor who avoids reminders and harm, even remarks such as complaining of the recipient's persistence, is guaranteed reward, identified here as Paradise.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r14.claim: The donor is promised security from future fear after death and from grief over worldly losses, since he rejoices in the afterlife.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r15.claim: The verse also supports preferring wealth to poverty, a question the commentary says it will explain later.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r2.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r2.claim: Giving without seeking repayment or thanks, and without reminding or publicizing the gift, is nobler for the giver and more comfortable for the recipient; seeking repayment makes the giver a trader unworthy of praise.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reads 74:6 as forbidding a gift given in expectation of a larger return.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says this verse concerns those who remain behind from jihad yet spend, while the preceding verse concerns those who go out themselves; Ibn Atiyya rejects this as unsupported conjecture.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya finds Ibn Zayd's allocation of this and the preceding verse to different groups manifestly speculative.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r6.claim: Mann is recounting a favor in order to enumerate it and reproach the recipient; another definition is talking about a gift until the recipient hears and is hurt.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r7.claim: Mann is a major sin; Muslim reports that it is among three whom God will neither regard nor purify and who face painful punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r8.claim: Ibn Umar transmits a Prophetic warning listing people barred from God's regard and from Paradise, including one who reminds others of what he gave.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262#2/r9.claim: One Muslim wording defines the mannan as someone who gives nothing except to hold it over the recipient.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سمرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r1.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura reports that ʿUthmān brought a thousand dinars for the army of hardship; the Prophet handled and kissed the money, praised ʿUthmān, and prayed God remember him for that day.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r2.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says he saw the Prophet raise his hands and pray that God be pleased with ʿUthmān; the prayer continued until dawn, when the verse was revealed.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r3.claim: The preceding verse broadly praised spending in God’s cause; this verse limits its reward to those who do not follow their gifts with reminders or harm, which invalidate charity’s reward as the next verse explains.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r4.claim: A giver should seek God’s face and reward, expect nothing from the recipient, and consider only whether the recipient deserves help; the Qurʾān quotes the righteous as saying they seek neither reward nor thanks.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r5.claim: Giving to obtain repayment or under pressure from a debt, grudge, or another’s intervention is not truly for God; accepted giving has God as its aim and its chief hoped-for reward.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:262/r6.claim: An illustrative exchange has a Bedouin praise ʿUmar in verse and demand clothes for his daughters and wife, even threatening departure and accountability; the report illustrates a gift sought for God rather than for the giver’s praise.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Uthman equipping the army of hardship with a thousand camels and their gear, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf giving four thousand dirhams in charity.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r2.claim: Mann is reminding a recipient of one's kindness; adha is acting superior to the recipient because of the gift; thumma marks the contrast between giving and refraining from reproach or harm.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:262-263/r3.claim: The reward clause lacks an expected fa despite its conditional meaning, suggesting the donors deserve it even without the stated condition, all the more when they fulfill it.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r1.claim: Mann is reminding a recipient of one's favor and treating it as a debt owed; people were told to forget their good deeds after doing them.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r2.claim: Adhā is acting superior to the recipient because of the gift.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r3.claim: Then marks the moral contrast: avoiding reproach and hurt is better than the act of giving, as steadfast faith is better than entering faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r4.claim: Their reward is their spending's recompense; they need not fear its reduction or punishment and need not grieve lost reward.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r5.claim: This verse says 'their reward' without fa because its relative clause is not conditional; the later verse includes the conditional sense.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129/r6.claim: The comparison to steadfastness after entering faith is phrased as a link to the verse 'then they remained steadfast.'

QASHANI:2:261-262/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:261-262/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:261-262/r4.claim: Charity is praised for obeying God's command, curing the donor's stinginess, and relieving the recipient; reproach violates the command and revives worse egoistic pride, conceit, and self-credit.

QASHANI:2:261-262/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:261-262/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:261-262/r5.claim: Hurt cancels the recipient's benefit and relief; reproach also humiliates them by asserting superiority and a debt, so either can nullify the gift.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p649#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p649#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p649#2/r4.claim: من can mean a measure or weight, blessing and favor, or the reproachful reminder of a gift; its underlying sense is cutting off a portion of one’s property for another.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p657/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p657/r5.speaker: مفسرون غير مسمين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p657/r5.claim: Reports connect the verse with ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, or ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and ʿUthmān; the latter gave four thousand dirhams at Tabūk and kept as much, while ʿUthmān supplied camels, a well, or a thousand dinars according to variants.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p657/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p657/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p657/r6.claim: The seed parable’s general promise is narrowed: reward belongs to spenders who do not follow their gift with reproach or injury, which nullify charity; seeking praise becomes ostentation, while seeking repayment makes the giver a trader rather than a benefactor.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r1.claim: Reproach is a grave sin; Muslim reports count the reproachful giver among three whom God will neither regard nor purify, and al-Nasāʾī says a giver who reproaches will not enter Paradise, with two other cases.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r2.claim: Then after في سبيل الله shows that an otherwise valid gift can be followed by what voids it; acceptance is conditional on avoiding reproach and harm, as the next verse clarifies.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r3.claim: The apparent rule covers reproach or harm by a donor toward a recipient in jihad equipment, other assistance, or ordinary giving, whether donor or recipient fights.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd limits this verse to people who stay behind and donate, while the preceding verse addresses those who go out with their persons and wealth; thus the conditions differ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r5.claim: Harm is broader than reproach; reproach is named first because donors often commit it, whether by boasting, publicizing the gift, insulting or complaining about the recipient, or forcing acknowledgment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam advises a donor who fears even a greeting would burden the recipient to refrain from greeting, if seeking God’s favor.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r7.claim: An anecdote says a woman asked Abū Usāma for a sincere warrior and mentioned her painful sores; he replied that she had hurt them before giving anything.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r8.claim: The reward clause is a predicate of الذين ينفقون; the subject is not construed conditionally, so the explanation continues that this fixed promise does not require a conditional result particle.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p658/r9.claim: The reward sentence explains the preceding established promise and therefore states a settled fact without فاء; making it a result clause would imply that entitlement depends on a preceding condition.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r1.claim: Another syntax makes الذين ينفقون the predicate of an omitted subject; Abū Ḥayyān rejects taking لهم أجرهم as a circumstantial clause and prefers an independent answer about whether and with whom they have reward.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r2.claim: ثم reflects the common delay before a hidden motive produces reproach; even reproach accompanying or following a gift has the same ruling as later reproach.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r3.claim: Zamakhsharī says ثم marks the superiority of abandoning reproach and harm over giving itself; Abū Ḥayyān says he knows no earlier authority for this recurrent grammatical claim.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p660/r4.claim: ما in ما أنفقوا may be relative with its object omitted or a verbal noun; the phrase also omits “reproach toward the recipient.” Abū Ḥayyān rejects readings that shift “no harm” to the donor or the no-fear promise to worldly poverty.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r1.claim: منا is the second object of يتبعون, with لا أذى coordinated to it.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r2.claim: Treating ولا أذى as an independent description of donors who are not themselves harmed is strained and makes the sentence a negative prohibition.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262#2/r3.claim: That rejected parse would require أذى without tanwin, as a noun built on fatḥ under the standard grammatical view.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r1.claim: الذين may be a nominative subject whose predicate is لهم أجرهم; it explains the preceding settled parable, so no conditional sense or fa is needed.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r2.claim: Alternatively, الذين is the predicate of an omitted subject, هم الذين ينفقون; then لهم أجرهم may be circumstantial or, preferably, an independent answer to an implied question about reward.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r3.claim: ثم marks rank rather than time: refraining from reproach and harm is better than the spending itself, as in ثم استقاموا.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r4.claim: The temporal ثم also fits ordinary practice: reproach and harm usually do not immediately follow a donation, though the same rule applies when they do.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r5.claim: ما may be a relative pronoun with omitted object suffix, ما أنفقوه, or a verbal noun meaning their spending, requiring no suffix.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r6.claim: After منا an understood phrase is omitted: reproach toward the recipient and no harm to him.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r7.claim: منّ means counting a favor; its underlying sense is cutting, extended to a gift because the giver cuts off part of his property for its recipient.

SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:262/r8.claim: The word also means reducing a right or a weighing measure; here منا is inflected like عصا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r1.claim: God praises those who give in His cause and then neither boast to recipients nor remind them of their gift in word or deed.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r2.claim: They do not mistreat beneficiaries in a way that cancels their earlier kindness; their reward is with God, they need not fear future terrors, and they will not grieve over lost family or worldly pleasures.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r6.claim: The Prophet warned of painful punishment for three people: one who flaunts what he gave, one who lets his garment trail, and a merchant who uses false oaths.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p693/r7.claim: A report says that a person disobedient to parents, one who flaunts charity, a habitual wine drinker, and a denier of divine decree do not enter Paradise; other transmitters report a similar version.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r1.claim: Another prophetic report lists the disobedient child, habitual wine drinker, and person who flaunts gifts among three whom God will not look upon at the Resurrection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r2.claim: A report through Mujāhid says habitual wine drinkers, those disobedient to parents, and those who flaunt gifts do not enter Paradise; other transmissions attribute related reports to Mujāhid from Abū Saʿīd and Abū Hurayra.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r1.claim: The text attributes the wealth to the spenders and stresses spending in God's way to encourage sincere care in preserving its reward.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r2.claim: Mann is reminding the recipient of one's gift, which cuts the relationship by looking down on the recipient; adhā is telling others in a way that humiliates the recipient.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r3.claim: Both conditions must be met: repeating no before injury as well as mann emphasizes that the absence of either fault is required for reward.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r4.claim: The reward is introduced without a causal conjunction to show that it is a generous, initial gift from God rather than a payment caused by their conduct; forbidden conduct forfeits it.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p516/r5.claim: God as their Lord nurtures and preserves donations until they grow beyond description; those rewarded need fear no loss or regret no omission because He supplies every fitting good.

DURR-FULL:v2p39/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r5.claim: God knew some people reproached recipients for their gifts, disliked this, and addressed it here.

DURR-FULL:v2p39/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r6.claim: Some funded a fighter or another recipient, then reproached and hurt him, claiming their gifts were for God's cause but not seeking God's reward.

DURR-FULL:v2p39/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r7.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r7.claim: The Prophet tells al-Bara that spending on one's family, children, and servant counts as charity and must not be followed by reproach or harm.

DURR-FULL:v2p39/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r8.claim: The Prophet says family expenses without extravagance or parsimony are spending in God's cause.

DURR-FULL:v2p39/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r9.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
DURR-FULL:v2p39/r9.claim: The Prophet says work is for God's cause when supporting young children, elderly parents, or oneself chastely; work for show or boasting follows Satan's path.

BURSEVI:v1p342/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p342/r1.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p342/r1.claim: Saʿdī's poem recounts ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz selling his precious gem-set ring during a famine and giving the proceeds to the needy rather than remain comfortable while citizens suffered.

BURSEVI:v1p342/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p342/r2.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p342/r2.claim: The poem praises preferring people's comfort over one's own and refusing to keep luxury while the poor are distressed.

BURSEVI:v1p342/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p342/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p342/r6.claim: The spenders put wealth in its proper place; ثم signals the high rank of adding restraint from boasting and harm after the gift.

BURSEVI:v1p342/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p342/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p342/r7.claim: Mann is reminding recipients of one's favor as if they now owe a debt; harm includes reproaching them for ingratitude, repeated requests, or annoyance.

BURSEVI:v1p342/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p342/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p342/r8.claim: Those who give without boasting or harm receive their reward from God, face no fear of future punishment, and do not grieve over worldly things left behind.

BURSEVI:v1p343/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p343/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p343/r1.claim: A story says Hasan ibn ʿAli sells Fatima's shirt for six dirhams, gives the money to a beggar, then arranges a deferred camel purchase and resale; the Prophet identifies the beggar, seller, and buyer as angels.

BURSEVI:v1p343/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p343/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p343/r2.claim: Some exegetes say the two verses concern ʿUthmān, who equipped the Tabuk army with a thousand camels and a thousand dinars, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who gave half his wealth.

BURSEVI:v1p343/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p343/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p343/r3.claim: The Prophet prayed that God be pleased with ʿUthmān; he blessed ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's retained and donated money, and both gave without boasting or hurting recipients.

BURSEVI:v1p343/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p343/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p343/r4.claim: One opinion compares boasting to hypocrisy and harm to ostentation.

BURSEVI:v1p343/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p343/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p343/r5.claim: Scholars differ on consequences: one view denies reward and assigns sin, Wahb denies both reward and sin, and another preserves the basic reward but removes multiplication and adds sin for boasting.

BURSEVI:v1p343/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p343/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p343/r6.claim: Although God may bestow favor on His servants, humans cannot boast: God's ownership and power are complete, while any virtue in a servant comes from God.

BURSEVI:v1p343/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p343/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p343/r7.claim: The recipient already feels humbled by need; displaying the gift further crushes the recipient and turns a benefit into harm and mistreatment.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r1.claim: The passage begins by explaining the proper manner of the previously praised spending: donors must not follow gifts with reminders of favor or injury to recipients.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r2.claim: Man originally means cutting, and injury means patronizing or boasting over recipients; man precedes injury because it occurs more often.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r3.claim: The word thumma signals the greater rank and distance between giving and avoiding reproach or harm; al-Intiṣāf instead reads it as prolonged persistence in avoiding them, which the author considers preferable.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r4.claim: Al-Intiṣāf’s interpretation makes thumma signify enduring continued conduct, as in steadfastness after initial commitment and lasting guidance, and preserves its core sense of temporal extension.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī, transmitting from al-Kalbī with an explicit reservation, says the verse was revealed about ʿUthmān and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf’s large charitable contributions.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r6.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān gave four thousand dirhams, half of his eight thousand savings, as a loan to God; the Prophet blessed both the gift and what he kept for his family.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r7.claim: ʿUthmān pledged to equip anyone lacking equipment on the Tabūk expedition, supplied a thousand camels with gear, and gave the Muslims his well of Rumah.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r8.claim: Abū Saʿīd says he saw the Prophet praying for ʿUthmān with raised hands until dawn, after which the verse about those who spend was revealed.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p33/r9.claim: The promise that donors have their reward with their Lord is restated for emphasis and honor; omitting an expected conditional fa suggests their inner good intention merits reward in itself.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34/r1.claim: The promise means fear and grief will be absent continuously, rather than merely denying that their absence itself will ever end.

ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r1.claim: The omission of fa avoids suggesting that spending itself is the true, sufficient cause of reward; God remains the real cause and acceptance depends on His conditions.

ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r2.claim: Minnet has two lexical senses: favor or blessing, and diminishing a gift by counting it or taking pride in it; the latter is intended here.

ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r3.claim: Ezā includes making a recipient recoil, complaining over a fault because of one's gift, insulting them, and throwing the gift in their face; Turkish minnet can cover both terms.

ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r4.claim: One should do good as a duty and forget it, since reward depends on intention; the Creator knows even when the recipient does not.

ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r5.claim: A report says Uthman gave a thousand camels with their equipment and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf gave four thousand dirhams to equip the Tabuk hardship army, and this verse was revealed in their honor.

ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264#2/r6.claim: The rule of the verse is general and not confined to the reported occasion of revelation.

ELMALILI:2:261-264/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264/r19.claim: Spending's reward is not automatic: only those who do not follow their gifts with reminders or hurt receive the promised reward with their Lord and have no fear or grief.

ELMALILI:2:261-264/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:261-264/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:261-264/r20.claim: Those donors fear only God and expect reward only from Him, so they have no other fear or grief and receive multiplied recompense for what they lose.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r1.claim: Repeating the description of those who spend emphasizes the importance of this quality.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains ثم as rank-order rather than elapsed time: leaving off reminders and harm is more exalted than the act of giving, which can gratify the donor's vanity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r3.claim: Mann originally meant favor or generosity, then came to mean recalling one's benefaction to its recipient; after charity it has that latter sense.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r4.claim: Mann in spending includes boasting to Muslims or those equipped for battle, but not praising a fighter's service or his people's contribution; poems by al-Ḥuraysh and ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās illustrate the distinction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p42/r5.claim: Harm means injuring recipients in word or deed; the discussion begins a poetic illustration by al-Nābigha.

TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r1.claim: Ittibāʿ means following or attaching something afterward; the commentary illustrates it with Pharaoh's followers and a curse attached to people.

TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r2.claim: Mann is mentioning a favor in a way that spoils it; its root sense is said to be cutting, as in an uncut reward.

TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r3.claim: Adhā is immediate harm or harm that is slight.

TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274#4/r4.claim: Fear is expectation of harm, while grief is distress over a harm that has occurred or is as if occurring.

TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r3.claim: The Prophet asks al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib about his generous support of his mother and says spending on one's household, child, and servant counts as charity if it is not followed by reminders or harm; al-Ḥākim's report is graded authentic.

TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r4.claim: Reports from both traditions establish that every act God approves is in His path and every expenditure in His path is charity.

TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r5.claim: Al-Qummī transmits the Prophet’s statement that one who does a believer a favor and then hurts him verbally or reminds him of it has nullified the charity.

TABATABAI:2:261-274/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r1.claim: The connected themes suggest this passage was revealed as one unit: spending grows seven hundredfold or more, sincere giving bears fruit, ostentation and reminders or harm ruin reward, good wealth should be given, the poor detained in God's path are recipients, and the reward is great.

TABATABAI:2:261-274/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r2.claim: The passage orders its teaching around purpose (giving for God, not people), manner (without reproach or injury), quality (good rather than bad wealth), recipient (the needy constrained in God's path), and reward.

ASAD-NOTES:2:262#n258/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:262#n258/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:262#n258/r1.claim: The literal wording is that donors should not follow up their spending with reminders or injury.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:262/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:262/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:262/r1.claim: The sure sign that charity is for God's pleasure is expecting no benefit, placing no burden of gratitude on the recipient, and not hurting them; such donors receive great reward and freedom from fear and grief.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:262/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:262/r2.speaker: Vâhidî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:262/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi reports that verse 262 came in connection with Uthman and Abdurrahman ibn Awf helping the army before Tabuk; Uthman equipped soldiers and Abdurrahman gave half his wealth.

QIRAAT-ER:2:262:23#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:262:23#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:262:23#1/r1.claim: The accusative makes khawf the ism of lā in the lā nāfiya lil-jins construction, with no change in meaning.

QIRAAT-ER:2:262:24#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:262:24#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:262:24#1/r1.claim: The pronoun hāʾ takes -hum rather than -him, a phonological variant with no semantic change.

STUDYQURAN:2:262/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:262/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:262/r1.claim: Pride in generosity or reminding recipients of their need destroys charitable giving’s merit; a decent word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by harm.

STUDYQURAN:2:262/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:262/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:262/r2.claim: R says one should speak kindly to poor people and forgive harm they may cause through rough manner or embarrassment.

STUDYQURAN:2:262/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:262/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:262/r3.claim: R says to forgive the poor if their requests cause trouble or discomfort.
